reason: The text demonstrates the opposite of the statement. When the Israelite people cry out to Yahweh (v.3) after twenty years of oppression, Yahweh responds by providing deliverance. The narrative shows Yahweh actively intervening for the entire nation of Israel: discomfiting Sisera and his forces before Barak (v.15), going out before Barak in battle (v.14), and subduing King Jabin of Canaan (v.23). These divine acts of military salvation are directed toward rescuing the oppressed people as a whole, not merely favoring their leaders. Deborah and Barak function as instruments through which Yahweh delivers the people—they are not the primary objects of divine care. The text consistently portrays Yahweh hearing and responding to the people's distress with empathy and intervention.
